question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q1e — Pressure Law Temperature Calculation
question.text:
In an experiment on a fixed mass of gas at constant volume, the pressure of the gas is 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa at a temperature of 25.0°C.

When the cylinder is heated, the pressure reaches 2.1 × 10⁵ Pa.

Calculate the temperature of the gas (in °C) at this new pressure.
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Step 1: Convert temperatures to Kelvin: T₁ = 25 + 273 = 298 K
Step 2: Apply pressure law P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂ → T₂ = T₁ × P₂/P₁ = 298 × (2.1/1.2) = 298 × 1.75 = 521.5 K
Step 3: Convert back to °C: θ₂ = 521.5 − 273 = 248.5°C (accept 248–249°C)

Common error: forgetting to convert °C to K before applying the ratio.

steps.label:
Given: P₁ = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa  |  θ₁ = 25°C  |  P₂ = 2.1 × 10⁵ Pa
Formula: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂ (constant volume, fixed mass)
Note: T must be in Kelvin. Convert: T(K) = θ(°C) + 273
Convert the initial temperature to Kelvin. (1 mark)
Calculate T₂ using the pressure law. (3 marks)
Convert T₂ back to degrees Celsius. (1 mark)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Convert °C to Kelvin: add 273. T = 25 + 273 = 298 K
T₂ = T₁ × (P₂ ÷ P₁). If T₁ = 298 K and ratio = 1.75, then T₂ = 298 × 1.75 = 521.5 K
Convert back to Celsius: subtract 273. θ = T(K) − 273
